# Common source collection: informed pre-code study

This study is frozen before the next private source-collection implementation
under the common frontend plan. It was authored after reading current parser,
finite Project/bundled loading, selected module-map loading, resolution/profile
contracts and prior real QFT study results. Codex authored it; exact deployment
and sampling are unavailable. It is informed development, not a blind benchmark.

Eight complete first projects retain ordinary functions and real rejection
candidates: ordinary finite main imports exact bundled std::transforms::qft2;
a two-module sized helper calls its private sibling; a never-called ownership-
invalid sibling; an external private import; a basis declaration currently
outside the sized projection; an earlier unsupported basis vs later malformed
module and the reverse order; and injection into the reserved std:: map scope.
No check has yet decided their actual outcome. All provided executable input
systems use at most two physical qubits. The existing finite checker compiles
all bundled declarations, including the retained four-bit mul2_mod15 library
body; this unchanged existing public-path traversal is distinguished from a
new generated or executed >3-width program. No maximum case is requested.

Every project has a schema-2 edition-2026 manifest. Selected CLI observations
supply explicit local modules and do not claim package-manifest loading or
implicit stdlib discovery. Reserved std injection is a deliberate negative,
not permission to shadow trusted primitive/bundled paths. Ordinary annotations
are absent; any checked effect must come from complete body checking.

The first fixed driver captures text/JSON check diagnostics and native argument
counts. Sized emit-proposal commands additionally retain exact untrusted output
bytes and their real JSON statuses, without native acceptance. The finite case
uses check only; no verified finite artifact is mislabelled as an untrusted
proposal. No expected failure is fabricated or substituted for actual output.
Ordering-sensitive source/profile failures are recorded rather than silently
regarded as interchangeable. These observations prove no program meaning.

A separate after phase may run the exact frozen source with a newly built CLI
only when the root authorizes that replay. It must preserve the entire baseline,
record new CLI/source identities and compare original stdout/stderr/exits/native
counts and proposal bytes. It records any meaningful diagnostic-order change;
no failed result grants fallback or automatic compatibility approval. Driver
commands are fixed, not selected from metadata or a recorded command list.

identity-before.json records current local HEAD and the distinct prior compiled
production commit reported by the parent. Record-only commits cannot attest a
newly compiled HEAD. The Rust, Lean-kernel, stdlib/manifest, native, CLI and current
contracts are retained by hash; a hash is identity, not theorem evidence.
Adopted edition-2026 QS/PR/RS and EXACT apply; both ordinary QLV1 scoped guarantees
remain protected. No new primitive, acceptance rule, Guardian interpretation,
source-preservation proof, broad guarantee or release completion is claimed.
